content.comment_body: I am considering using [product_name] for automatic switching between a generator and the public power supply. Is it possible for the switching action to occur when there is a power outage, since [product_name] would also lose its power source at that moment? How can the circuit program function without power supplied to [product_name]? Please provide clarification or suggestions for making this possible.
Hello, Without power, the device cannot operate. You could consider using relays with changeover contacts, so that in case of a power failure, the normally closed contact can trigger other actions.

You could use a 24V DC supply sourced from the generator's battery to power [product_name], and obtain power for your main changeover contactor from the generator output. However, you would need the [product_name] version capable of running at 12/24V DC.
Using a small UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply) to provide power to the 230V AC version of [product_name] and its directly connected relays could be a solution.
Hi, This resource might be useful: Automatic System Transfer with [product_name]. [url]

analysis.insight_summary: Users are discussing whether an automatic changeover between a generator and public power supply can be effectively managed with [product_name] during a mains failure, recognizing that loss of power to the device prevents operation. Suggestions include alternative power supplies, choosing the suitable version, or integrating a UPS to ensure continued device operation during power outages.
analysis.user_expectations: The user anticipates [product_name] will execute automatic changeover switching reliably, even during main power failure, maintaining uninterrupted control logic performance.
